newsitem.title: USA: Calif. high court limits state use of contractors.
newsitem.headline: Calif. high court limits state use of contractors.

text.p: California's Supreme Court on Thursday upheld decades-old restrictions barring state agencies from hiring private contractors to perform work that can be done as well and as cheaply by state employees.

The state's high court ruled that the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans) is bound by court precedents limiting the state's authority to contract with private entities to perform services the state has "historically or customarily" performed.
"The civil service mandate forbids private contracts for work that the state itself can perform 'adequately and competently,'" the court's majority said in a ruling issued in San Francisco.
The state Supreme Court decision stemmed from a 1986 lawsuit by a labor group representing state engineers.
The group asked the courts to bar Caltrans from contracting with private entities for state highway projects, work traditionally done by state civil service employees.
Loren McMaster, an attorney for the group, said the ruling was a "tremendous victory" for state workers, and a set back for California Governor Pete Wilson's privatization efforts.
Caltrans said the ruling threatened to delay nearly $500 million in highway projects.
